messages:
Ava: sharing a quick mock — thinking about reorganizing the eval-run filters into compact pills instead of the current left rail list. aim is denser density for power users, but worried about discoverability and a11y. mock: https://figma.redwood/xyz :eyes:
Sam: looks good, thanks. quick q — are these mutually exclusive (segmented control) or multi-select chips?
Ava: multi-select chips. user story: run -> filter by tags + status + model. want to show active filters and counts.
Luis: small concern: counts on every pill will create visual noise and push content. maybe show counts only on hover or in a tooltip?
Grace: accessibility nit: contrast on the selected pill is borderline. also keyboard focus ring is missing in the mock. we need focus-visible, and aria-pressed or aria-checked semantics for toggled chips.
Maya: +1 to Grace. Also consider a clear all affordance that is in the toolbar, not inside each chip. cheaper to implement and less clutter.
Ava: good calls. tradeoffs: 1) pills + counts inline (compact but noisy) 2) pills + counts in tooltip (cleaner but discoverability hit) 3) segmented single-select for status only + chips for tags. thoughts?
Sam: option 3 seems pragmatic. status is often single value. tags are multi. keeps mental model simple.
Luis: agree. for counts we could show a subtle badge only when count > 0, with muted color and aria-label="n results". hide on small widths to avoid wrapping.
Grace: sample aria suggestion:
```
<button role="checkbox" aria-checked="true" aria-label="Approved — 24 results">Approved</button>
```
Also add :focus-visible outline and ensure 3:1 contrast for non-critical UI and 4.5:1 for interactive states.
Ava: love the aria example. does anyone feel strongly that pills should be in the left rail vs top-of-table? our data shows people glance at top filters more.
Maya: top-of-table is standard for searches. left rail is OK for persistent dashboards but takes vertical space. go top-of-table for compact flows.
Luis: implementation note: we can reuse the existing Chip component but need to extend with optional badge and keyboard support. I can prototype tomorrow.
Sam: microcopy: instead of "All" maybe use "Any/All"? confusion risk. what do we mean when multiple tags are selected — is it AND or OR?
Ava: good call — we need explicit language. UX decision: tags = OR; filters across groups = AND. I'll add a small helper text: "Selected tags match any; filters across categories are combined."
Grace: also add tooltip that explains keyboard shortcuts: "← → to navigate chips, Space to toggle". include visible focus targets for low-vision users.
rollout-bot: deploy queued: update/chips-a11y #789 — staging in 2h
Maya: QA checklist for this rollout: keyboard nav, screenreader announcement for toggle ("Approved filter applied, 24 results"), responsive collapse behavior, and test with >20 active filters to ensure overflow UX.
Ava: thanks all — action items: Luis prototype chips + optional badge (due tomorrow), Grace will write a11y acceptance criteria, Sam will do copy tweaks, Maya will own QA. I'll update the figma and we can do a 15m sync Friday. :thumbsup:
